preview.title: Outpatient treatment of COVID-19 and incidence of post-COVID-19 condition over 10 months (COVID-OUT): a multicentre, randomised, quadruple-blind, parallel-group, phase 3 trial
preview.preview: COVID-OUT reported a lower hazard of later clinician-diagnosed Long COVID after metformin began during acute infection, but this result remains provisional while an indexed correction is reconciled. The result does not establish treatment benefit for people who already have Long COVID. The long-term analysis used a selected follow-up group. Cumulative-incidence percentages are withheld because the acquired source reports conflicting control values.
preview.decisiveLimit: Correction indexed as PMID 37666258; exact amended content not yet reconciled. The acquired source reports conflicting control cumulative-incidence percentages. Reader-facing percentages are withheld, and the source-reported hazard ratio remains provisional on correction HOLD.

preview.title: Metformin on the Presence of COVID-19 Symptoms 6 Months after Infection: The ACTIV-6 Randomized Clinical Trial.
preview.preview: This randomized prevention trial did not meet its efficacy threshold for symptoms attributed to COVID-19 or death at six months. The secondary clinician-diagnosis point estimate favored metformin, but its interval included no difference and does not replace the primary result. The study had few observed events and missing follow-up responses. These findings concern treatment during acute infection, not starting metformin to treat an established Long COVID illness.
preview.decisiveLimit: Publisher shows corrected/typeset 9 July 2026; NCBI metadata links earlier preprint (PMID 40832427) as UpdateOf. No separate correction notice retrieved. Full correction search remains bounded.

preview.title: Nirmatrelvir-Ritonavir and Symptoms in Adults With Postacute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 Infection: The STOP-PASC Randomized Clinical Trial
preview.preview: A 15-day nirmatrelvir–ritonavir course did not significantly improve the selected symptom outcomes in STOP-PASC. Participants already had long COVID, so the question differed from acute treatment or prevention. Symptoms improved in both groups. The small, selected, single-center population limits broader conclusions, and later trials still require full-text reconciliation. The source includes a correction to Figure 2.
preview.decisiveLimit: July 22 2024 correction repositions dashed lines in Figure 2. Current PMC article explicitly includes correction.

preview.title: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot study of metformin as an adjunctive therapy in Parkinson's disease
preview.preview: The pilot did not demonstrate a between-group clinical benefit on UPDRS total, despite improvement within the metformin arm.
preview.decisiveLimit: Short duration, small sample, one metformin dose, single center/Middle East population; metabolic rate and dietary habits not measured/controlled; further biomarker and vitamin B12/lipid/glucose assessment desirable (pp8–9).

preview.title: Metformin-improved cognitive impairment in patients with schizophrenia is correlated with activation of tricarboxylic acid cycle and restored functional connectivity of hippocampus
preview.preview: The report describes exploratory metabolic and brain-connectivity findings, but the accepted record has no current between-arm cognitive efficacy estimate.
preview.decisiveLimit: Small sample, incomplete blood/MRI time points, potential confounding and medication-adherence bias, short follow-up, mechanism incompletely explored (pp10–11). Methods explicitly use unadjusted exploratory correlation/interaction P values and last observation carried forward for missing TCA/cognition; MRI not imputed (p4).
